correctness.rationale: The eroded-simplex formula follows exactly from affine barycentric coordinates. The width coefficient is then reduced to the Euclidean radius of the polar difference body. The proof identifies that polar with the zonotope generated by barycentric gradients, so its radius is the largest subset-gradient norm and also \(1/w(S)\). The equality-direction argument uses equality in the subset maximum and Cauchy--Schwarz, and the complementary-face interpretation follows from exact vertex evaluation differences. All quantifiers require only a nondegenerate simplex, \(0<W<w(S)\), and a unit direction; no regularity assumption enters the main theorem.

value.rationale: The source reduces all finite partial-plank coverings to a directional erosion quantity and then can solve a higher-dimensional simplex only when a facet altitude happens to equal the width. The new theorem evaluates that reduction target exactly for every simplex and exposes its full extremal geometry. It also shows that regular simplices outside the source's solved altitude class already saturate the Bang homothetic bound at the erosion stage, locating the remaining obstruction in the conversion from erosion to one-plank geometry. This is a structural lemma for an active covering problem, not a routine parameter substitution or finite recomputation.
